full_judgment: 12. As to the other ground that inclusion of the house in the 'ka' list of abandoned houses during pendency of CR No. 72 of 1984 and 806 of 1986 was illegal it appears from clause (b) of sub-section (1) of section 5 of the Abandoned Buildings (Supplementary Provisions) Ordinance 1985, that if a suit, appeal, application or other legal proceedings is pending before any court, before the date of publication of the list in the official Gazette in which vesting in or possession of the Govt. of the building as abandoned property has been called in question in any manner, such property is to be excluded from such list. We have already noticed that petitioner filed suit only for specific performance of contract without challenging the abandoned character of the property or taking over of the same by the Govt. as abandoned property. So there was no illegality in the inclusion of the house in the 'ka' list of the abandoned houses. In the case of CQMH Md. Ayub vs. Bangladesh reported in 47 DLR (AD) 71 our above view finds support. In view of the same Court of Settlement rightly found that petitioners failed to discharge the presumption under section 5(2) of the said Ordinance.
